Messages.Author: Charles Richard Robb
Messages.Body:
If ann acting minion plays Strike: Combat ends. Untap this vampire.,
can the blocking minion also play the same card to untap or can no more
combat cards be played once combat ends?

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <3oaer4$k...@nntp.msstate.edu>,


Certainly no more cards can be played once combat ends, but even more
so (and without logic), combat ends as soon as the strike hits the
table (rather than when the strike resolves), preventing the
blocking minion from choosing a strike at all.
--

Messages.Author: Duncan A McEwen
Messages.Body:
Here is some more good ideas.

I really can't understand why the packaging could not just be changed.
In my oppion it will save WoTC money because they wont have to change
the card plates or presses or what ever. The packaging is going to change
anyhow right?

Ok, if WoTC is going to change the backs then offer a trade in program.
Anyone remeber antiquites? Do to the problems with sorting in that set
WoTC offered 20 cents per card or a trade for an equal rarity. I would
trade in all my Jyhad cards for V:TES cards in that situation and be very
content (even thought I don't like the new name) This way the old players
and the new players could both be happy. And if people don't turn there
cards in they shouldn't complain.

Lastly, a few reasons that haven't gotten much air time not to change the
backs. It will look silly. I mean I think a deck with both kind of cards
will just look silly and even confuse people. Say someone see me playing
a mixed deck. And ask why the cards have differnt backs. This becomes
instant bad press for WoTC. Something to deffinatly think about.

WoTC has supported us in the past (see antiquites). I hope they don't
stop now. I really like Jyhad and want to keep playing but wont if
the card back thing goes through.
Thanks for the time,
Duncan McEwen
